questions.question:
**Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. The olive tree grows slowly yet lives a long time.

B. The normal lifespan of an olive tree is 300-400 years, but olive trees as ancient as 3000 years have been discovered.

C. The olive is a well-known Mediterranean-native evergreen tree whose fruit and oil are used in cuisine and cooking.

D. As a result, the olive tree is known as the 'immortal tree' in mythology and botany.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"CABD."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph discusses the olive tree, its slow growth, long lifespan, and culinary uses. So the first sentence must be C.
 
• The olive tree is known as the "immortal tree" due to its longevity. So, A follows C.
 
• The normal lifespan of an olive tree is 300-400 years, but some have been found to be as ancient as 3000 years. So B follows A.
 
• The paragraph follows a logical progression, starting with a description of the olive tree and ending with its mythological significance. So the last sentence must be D.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let us discuss other options:
 
 
• Option 1 (CDAB) starts with a description of the olive tree but then jumps to its mythological significance before discussing its lifespan and culinary uses.
 
• Option 3 (DBCA) starts with the olive tree's lifespan but then jumps to its culinary uses before discussing its growth and mythological significance.
 
• Option 4 (ABCD) follows the same progression as the correct answer but with a different sentence order.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

The article had not been posted by Mr. Gupta.

options.text: Mr. Gupta had not posted the article.
Mr. Gupta has not posted the article.
Mr. Gupta have not been posted the article.
Mr. Gupta still had not posted the article.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Mr. Gupta had not posted the article."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Past Perfect Tense(Negative) and Passive Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Past Perfect Tense from Passive voice to Active voice:
 
 
• To convert a sentence from passive to active voice, switch the positions of the subject and object and make the verb past participle form.
 
• Structure__: Subject + had not + past participle (V3) + object __(Active Voice)__

 Object + had not + been + past participle (V3) + (by + subject) __(Passive Voice)__ 
 
 
• Example: *Disha had not arranged the things. *(Active Voice)

 * The things had not been arranged by Disha.** *(Passive Voice)
 
 
 
 
 
• Active voice puts the subject (Mr. Gupta) as the doer of the action (posting the article).
 
• **"Had not been posted"** becomes** "had not posted"** in active voice.
 
• The sentence is now clear and concise, with a specific subject performing the action.
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question:
**Direction: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. So the problems of India should not be viewed as the failure of this great nation.

B. The uniqueness of this nation lies in its unity in diversity due to which there are problems here and there at times.

C. India, a very large country with many religions, many mini-cultures and many languages, has been achieving success in all fields.

D. But even small countries with monolithic societies have more problems than this second largest country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"CBDA."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sentence C **introduces the topic of India's success despite its diversity. So, C is the first sentence.
 
• **Sentence B** explains the uniqueness of India's diversity and how it can lead to occasional problems. So, B follows C.
 
• **Sentence D **provides a comparison to emphasize that India's problems are not as significant as some may think. So, D follows B.
 
• **Sentence A **concludes the paragraph by reminding readers that India's successes should not be overlooked. So, A must be the last sentence.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"****DBAC" **starts with the comparison in sentence D, which may confuse readers about the main topic.
 
• **"CADB"** places sentence A too early in the paragraph, disrupting the flow of ideas.
 
• **"BDAC"** begins with sentence B, which may not provide enough context for readers to understand the topic.
